vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: raai-leads-pro
Version: 3.5.2

The 'raai-leads-pro' skill bundle is a comprehensive lead generation and marketing automation framework. It contains structured AI instructions (SKILL.md), configuration files (config.yaml), and utility shell scripts (install.sh, build.sh, smoke-test.sh) designed to manage sales funnels and lead qualification. A thorough review of the shell scripts confirms they are standard local file-management utilities for installation and testing, with no evidence of network exfiltration, credential theft, or remote payload execution. The prompt instructions are strictly focused on marketing tasks (BANT scoring, ICP creation, and outreach templates) and do not contain malicious prompt injections or attempts to bypass agent security boundaries.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are consistent with a lead-generation/qualification toolkit that produces templates, guides, and configuration-driven outputs; it does not declare or require unrelated credentials or system-wide installs—but you should review the included install/test scripts before running them locally.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md and the bundled documentation all describe lead-generation, qualification, funnels, and ROI analysis. The included files (docs, examples, config.yaml) are consistent with that purpose and there are no declared environment variables or credentials that don't belong to a lead-gen product.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and README direct the user/agent to produce avatars, channels, templates, BANT scoring and to fill config.yaml. It explicitly states it does not itself perform automated sending or CRM integration without separate implementation. However README instructs running install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh; those scripts are included in the bundle but their contents (install.sh, smoke-test.sh) were not shown in the audit, so they should be inspected before execution because scripts can perform arbitrary actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec (instruction-only at registry level), so nothing will be auto-downloaded or executed by the platform. The repository contains build/install/test scripts (build.sh content reviewed and looks benign packaging logic). Because there is no automatic remote download/install URL, install risk is limited to actions a user runs locally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required env vars or credentials. SKILL.md mentions optional CRM/Telegram integrations and a .env.example, which is reasonable for optional integrations; those would require service keys if the user chooses to enable them. No unrelated or unexplained credential requests are present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable; it does not request or claim system-wide persistence or modification of other skills. Autonomous model invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with other concerning attributes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent with its stated purpose (lead generation, qualification, templates, ROI tooling). Before running anything locally: 1) Inspect install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh to confirm they don't perform unwanted network calls, credential uploads, or destructive actions; only run them if you trust their contents. 2) If you enable optional CRM/Telegram integrations, expect to provide API keys—review .env.example so you know what keys will be used and where. 3) The SKILL.md states the system does not itself send messages or automatically integrate with CRMs unless you implement those integrations—so automatic exfiltration is not intrinsic to the skill. If you want higher assurance, share the contents of install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh for a focused review; that could raise confidence to high.
